## Natural history notes

A medium-sized butterfly characterized by dark brown to black wings crossed by bold red-orange bands, with white spots near the forewing tips and a mottled brown-and-black underside that provides camouflage when the wings are closed. In Florida, it is found in gardens, parks, forest edges, hammocks, roadsides, fields, and other sunny or semi-open habitats where nectar plants and host plants occur. Adults feed on nectar, sap, rotting fruit, and moisture from damp ground, while the caterpillars feed mainly on nettles and related plants, often sheltering inside folded leaves.
